title: Cross-functional priority shift brief + Q&A (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a scratchpad for an internal announcement and all-hands talking points about the upcoming temporary cross-functional priority shift. Intended audience: all Redwood employees, with targeted manager/exec talking points for team syncs and 1:1s.

Goals of comms:
- Explain why we are shifting short-term priorities (consolidate effort for Q2 delivery and capacity constraints).
- Be explicit about scope, timeline, and expected impacts on hiring/roadmaps.
- Give managers a lightweight Q&A to use in team meetings and 1:1s.
- Surface where to escalate questions (who owns what).

High-level framing (for CEO/Head of Product use):
- TL;DR: We need to temporarily reallocate focus to a few cross-cutting initiatives (infra resilience, billing accuracy, and dedicated pilot rollout) to protect reliability and revenue velocity. This is a 6–8 week focused effort; roadmap items not in scope will be paused or deprioritized.
- Why now: recent usage patterns + billing reconciliation issues + customer readiness for Dedicated pilots create a near-term risk to revenue/customer trust. A small, timeboxed cross-functional push reduces that risk.
- Outcome we expect: higher stability, clearer commercial commitments for Dedicated, and fewer billing regressions.

Channels & timing (proposed):
- Phase 1 (today): Email + short intranet post announcing intent and where to find manager notes.
- Phase 2 (within 48h): Manager sync pack + Slack AMA (execs online for 30m).
- Phase 3 (this week): Doc with prioritized list and owner matrix on Confluence.
- All-hands segment: 5–7min CEO framing + 5min CTO tactical overview + 10min Q&A.

Core message (for email/intranet):
[Subject] Prioritizing work to secure Q2 availability and Dedicated pilot success
Body (short): Over the next ~6–8 weeks we are focusing company effort on three operational priorities: 1) stabilize serving runtime under current load patterns, 2) fix outstanding billing reconciliation flows, and 3) support the Dedicated pilot readiness checklist. Managers will receive a package to run team-level decisions. We expect most product roadmap work to be paused or deferred; individual contributors may shift for short windows. We will update weekly in the product channel.

Manager talking points (bullet-ready):
- You will receive a team-specific guidance doc by EOD tomorrow.
- Please prioritize tickets tagged "q2-priority-shift"; pause other work after a short handoff (document what you paused).
- If you have open hiring offers, please coordinate with People Ops before rescinding or delaying start dates.
- Escalations: Diego A. for infra triage, Aisha K. for billing/customer-impact decisions, Jonas P. for Dedicated pilot gating.

Anticipated employee Q&A (draft answers):
Q: Is this a hiring freeze?
A: Not a blanket freeze. We're asking hiring managers to pause non-critical requisitions for ~8 weeks while we evaluate headcount vs. critical operational needs. People Ops will review exceptions within 48h.

Q: Will my performance review / comp be affected?
A: No. This is a prioritization action, not a change to compensation or evaluation cycles. Reviews and comp cycles continue as planned.

Q: How will paused projects be handled?
A: Teams should document status (owner, next steps, blockers) in the pause-log doc and move code to safe branches. Product managers will own the re-prioritization list.

Q: Can ICs opt out?
A: We expect team-level alignment; if you have strong reasons to stay on a paused project (customer commitments, legal), flag in your 1:1 and managers will raise exceptions.

Q: How long will this last?
A: Our working assumption is 6–8 weeks. We will reassess at the 4-week mark.

Open/soft questions to resolve (notes to self):
- Need a clear sentence about contractor/agency work — are agency contracts in scope? (TODO: ask Legal / Finance)
- Exact wording re: offers that are already accepted (start dates within 30 days) — People Ops needs a decision.
- Confirm org-level exceptions for sales/customer-facing roles (likely exempt) — ping Sales Ops.
- Who will staff the Slack AMA? Need 2 execs + 2 SMEs (Diego + Aisha penciled).

Operational checklist for comms pack (owners):
- One-pager for managers (me) — include sample messages and pause-log template.
- Confluence prioritized list + owner matrix (Jonas).
- Slack AMA announcement & scheduling (Comms).
- All-hands slide (CEO + CTO bullets) (Design + Product comms).

Tone guidance (very important):
- Be transparent and pragmatic. Avoid absolutes like "hiring freeze" if we can say "pause on non-critical hires."
- Emphasize temporary, timeboxed nature and available exceptions.
- Lead with customer/prod risk and fairness to teams (we're protecting product reliability and revenue).

Quick message snippets (for managers to reuse):
- "We’re focusing company effort on a short, timeboxed set of operational priorities to reduce customer risk and ensure Dedicated pilot readiness. I’ll share which of our work items will be paused and who will take over."
- "If you have an accepted offer starting within 30 days, please forward to People Ops; do not assume the start will be delayed without confirmation."

Next steps (for me):
- Finalize manager one-pager and pause-log template by 2026-02-26 EOD.
- Lock names for Slack AMA and send calendar invites by 2026-02-27.
- Draft intranet/email and run by Diego & Aisha for technical/billing wording.
- Prep 2 slides for all-hands draft and send to Exec comms for feedback.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep it short for managers; they will edit.
- Avoid heavy legal phrasing in initial announcement.
- Track feedback in the Confluence page linked above.

Random checklist:
- [ ] Confirm agency contract scope with Finance
- [ ] People Ops exception policy doc link
- [ ] Publish pause-log template

End of scratchpad.
